result.instructions:
These tools operate a real BIM app. The app, not you, makes each change and checks it; it has no AI inside.
Read the grid with bim_lines before proposing. A bay is the difference of two line positions (pos), in metres, in the building's own frame.
bim_try_shift makes the change on a fresh copy of the building and returns the app's report. If the change adds new problems the app undoes it and says why ("stopped_by_gate"). Nothing is ever saved.
Treat a stopped or refused result as bad. You may try again up to 2 times; if the request cannot be met without a bad result, decline and tell the user why. Do not keep a bad change and add a note.
A row marked NOT_JUDGED was not checked: say so. Never call a result safe, compliant or OK.
Always tell the user what the report lists under notChecked. Load capacity is never checked; a structural engineer has the last word.

tools.name: bim_lines
tools.description: Read a building's grid: every grid line's id (gx0, gx1, … along x; gy0, gy1, … along y) and its position in metres in the building's own frame, plus the structural system, the material, the number of girders and the building's rotation in degrees. Opens a fresh copy of the building; takes about 10 to 40 seconds. Changes nothing.

tools.name: bim_try_shift
tools.description: Shift one grid line, and every later line on the same axis, by a distance in metres (positive = towards higher positions). Only the bay just before that line changes width; the rest of the building travels with it. The app makes the change, checks it (overlaps, beam spans against their limit, doors and windows against their walls) and returns its report: what changed, each check before and after, and what was not checked. If the change adds new problems the app undoes it and returns stopped_by_gate with the reason. Opens a fresh copy each time; nothing is saved.

building.description: The building name, as in bim_lines.

line.description: The grid line to shift, e.g. "gx6".

move.description: The distance in metres, e.g. 1.824. Negative moves towards lower positions.
